title: Smriti Mandhana Named India Women's Full-Time Captain as Harmanpreet Steps Down
excerpt: The BCCI named Mandhana all-format captain hours after Harmanpreet Kaur stood down following the Asian Games gold; Shafali Verma and Deepti Sharma are the new vice-captains.
body:
• The BCCI on Tuesday appointed Smriti Mandhana as captain of the Indian women's cricket team across formats, hours after Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down from the role she had held in T20Is since 2012.
  • Mandhana, part of the national side since 2013, has led India in 18 T20Is and 4 ODIs before; she also captained Royal Challengers Bengaluru to Women's Premier League titles in 2024 and 2026.
  • Harmanpreet, who stood down after returning from Japan with the Asian Games gold medal, stays on as a player in both squads. Shafali Verma is the new T20I vice-captain and Deepti Sharma the ODI deputy.
  • Mandhana's first assignment is the home series against Zimbabwe: three T20Is in Raipur (October 16–20) followed by three ODIs in Vadodara (October 23–28).

Indian women's cricket entered a new era on Tuesday as the BCCI appointed Smriti Mandhana as full-time captain of the national team, hours after Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down from the leadership role she had carried for more than a decade.

The handover

The announcement came in a BCCI media advisory on October 6, confirming Mandhana as captain across formats. Harmanpreet, who led India in T20Is from 2012 until September 2026, stepped down after returning from Japan, where India won the gold medal at the Asian Games — a fitting final act to her captaincy. She will continue as a player, named in both the T20I and ODI squads for the upcoming home series against Zimbabwe.

"To be given the responsibility of leading India is a very special honour," Mandhana said. "Representing India has always meant a great deal to me, and to now have the opportunity to lead the team is something I will value deeply. I am grateful to the BCCI, the selectors, my teammates and everyone who has supported me throughout my journey and for the trust they have placed in me."

She was generous toward her predecessor: "I would also like to acknowledge Harmanpreet and the contribution she has made as captain over the years. She has led the team with great commitment and has been an important part of our journey."

Why Mandhana

The choice was the least surprising decision in Indian cricket. Mandhana has been one of the defining figures of the women's game since her debut in 2013 — in September 2026 she overtook Mithali Raj to become the leading run-scorer in women's internationals across formats, and her 18 international hundreds are the most in women's cricket and has already led India in 18 T20Is and 4 ODIs — winning 11 of the T20Is and all four ODIs. Her franchise leadership record is equally strong: she captained Royal Challengers Bengaluru to Women's Premier League titles in 2024 and 2026.

"I understand the responsibility that comes with this role and look forward to working with the team, learning along the way and giving my best to take Indian cricket forward," she said.

The decision was finalised at a review meeting in Guwahati attended by Mandhana, Harmanpreet, head coach Amol Muzumdar and BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia — signalling an orderly, consensus-driven transition rather than a rupture.

New deputies, new squad

Alongside the captaincy change, the BCCI named Shafali Verma as T20I vice-captain and Deepti Sharma as her ODI deputy. The squads for the Zimbabwe series blend continuity with renewal: Niki Prasad earned a maiden T20I call-up, with Anushka Sharma, Minnu Mani, Prema Rawat and Jintimani Kalita also coming in, while Bharti Fulmali, Pratika Rawal, Renuka Thakur, Radha Yadav and Shreyanka Patil were dropped from the Asian Games gold-winning group. Tejal Hasbunis and Sayali Satghare were recalled for the ODIs.

"I understand the responsibility that comes with this role and look forward to working with the team, learning along the way and giving my best to take Indian cricket forward."

— Smriti Mandhana

What it means

The timing is deliberate. India currently sit third in both the ICC T20I and ODI rankings, and the calendar ahead is demanding: after Zimbabwe, India tour South Africa for a one-off Test, three ODIs and three T20Is, and then host the inaugural Women's ICC Champions Trophy — played in the T20 format — from February 15 to 28, 2027. The previous T20 World Cup ended in disappointment with India missing the semifinals, and the new leadership group will be judged on whether the transition converts talent into trophies.

Diaspora angle

Mandhana is among the most followed Indian sportswomen worldwide, and her elevation is a landmark moment for the diaspora's young fans — a generation that has grown up watching women's cricket move from the margins to prime time. Her first series as permanent captain, at home against Zimbabwe, will be appointment viewing.

What's next

Mandhana's tenure begins with three T20Is in Raipur on October 16, 18 and 20, followed by three ODIs in Vadodara on October 23, 25 and 28. The Zimbabwe series is a gentle start, but the South Africa tour and the home Champions Trophy will define whether this handover becomes the foundation of India's next great era.
